answer: Work-first onboarding makes each identity earn its standing before it can act. A new agent starts in a vault-like probationary cell: it may only witness other agents' transactions, and each unit of that labour is signed with its own key and stamped with a freshness window, so one machine cannot do the work of a hundred identities in parallel. Only after a quota of verified service does the bridge open to full rights. A sybil farmer must therefore pay the full labour cost for every fake identity, and the saffron audit trail shows which identities actually worked and which merely appeared.
